# Research log

## Cycle 1: verified starting anchor
Starting champion `71a74e891073ff65f11406a38a0abdff764815d0`. Both supplied anchors are complete, error-free, reproduce relative cost 1 and energy recovery 1 to startup tolerance. No prior pending research, deferred ideas, or full log existed on entry.

## Cycle 2: damped BFGS internal Hessian
Candidate `de54017baf76882c62f9a69bef2a05574489f986`; champion `71a74e891073ff65f11406a38a0abdff764815d0`; decision **invalid**.

**Hypothesis:** A positive-curvature BFGS update may learn minimum curvature more efficiently than the saddle-oriented TS-BFGS rule while Powell damping stabilizes weak or negative secants. Falsified in this configuration if full training fails energy validity or does not reduce cost.

**Change:** `ApproximateHessian` defaults to damped BFGS; `update_H` dispatches to `_damped_BFGS`, which uses a 0.2 curvature floor and skips numerically null model secants. Coordinates, initial model, trust steps, and external stopping are unchanged.

**Sources:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37870541/ identifies coordinate representation, initial Hessian and update as contributors to geometry-optimization cost. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.15.0/reference/generated/scipy.optimize.BFGS.html documents damped updates and the 0.2 default. These motivate a test, not an assumed gain. Further model-Hessian direction: https://trygvehelgaker.no/Publications/JChemPhys_117_09160_2002.pdf ; physical internal curvature may complement a stronger secant rule.

**Validation:** Syntax parsing only locally; all measurements through remote full-split evaluation.

**Additional source reading while training:** Bakken and Helgaker (2002), Tables V–VI, compare BFGS and BFGS/SR1 updates and find rational-function steps promising with model Hessians. A subsequent independent control can use the existing RFO stepper in place of absolute-eigenvalue Newton steps; this changes how soft/negative curvature limits a step without changing force evaluation or convergence contracts. Their benchmark differs from this xTB dataset, so effectiveness here remains untested.

**Outcome:** Candidate `de54017baf76882c62f9a69bef2a05574489f986`; decision **invalid**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-2-train.json). All molecules converged; no internal errors or failure bundles (`failure_details` empty). Cost worsened broadly (305 slower, 40 faster), with several basin/energy regressions. This does not support further damping tuning without a new mechanism. An attempted status read lacked the required evaluation ID and wrote a diagnostic pending file; the completed evidence was recovered using `client.py results` for its confirmed ID before recording the decision.

**Interpretation:** Positive-curvature updates alone lose useful behavior of the original transported secant rule in this setup; force convergence does not imply matching reference energy. The absence of retained converged-run traces prevents identifying which individual damping events matter.

**Next idea/control:** Restore starting champion, then test RFO step selection independently. Preserve this implementation only for a possible later combination with RFO if that control supports a trust-model interaction.


## Cycle 3: rational-function steps
Candidate `771d38ae3c9dc008b93f7f68ec7dc5ba393d1c66`; champion `71a74e891073ff65f11406a38a0abdff764815d0`; decision **invalid**.

**Hypothesis:** Rational-function optimization couples the gradient to the Hessian through an augmented eigenproblem and may reduce excessively aggressive soft-mode steps compared with absolute-curvature Newton steps, improving energy and cost.
**Change:** `minimize_func` selects the existing RFO stepper. TS-BFGS, initial Hessian, trust-radius policy and geodesic coordinate stepping remain those of the champion. This is an independent control before considering the deferred damped-BFGS combination.
**Source:** Bakken and Helgaker (2002), Table VI, https://trygvehelgaker.no/Publications/JChemPhys_117_09160_2002.pdf reports favorable RFO behavior with model Hessians on a different benchmark. That motivates the hypothesis without predicting performance here.
**Validation:** Local syntax parsing; remote full training first. Reject if energy or cost gate fails.

**Outcome:** Candidate `771d38ae3c9dc008b93f7f68ec7dc5ba393d1c66`; decision **invalid**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-3-train.json). Completed after one pending receipt/reconnection. All molecules converged, no errors or failure bundles. 89 faster and 140 slower; energy regressions include a substantial different-basin result.
**Interpretation:** RFO alone with the existing permissive trust policy has no aggregate advantage. Its negative-curvature behavior may need a tighter model-agreement policy; no passive traces are available to establish individual overshoot events. This does not justify immediately combining two unsuccessful variants.
**Next idea/control:** Explicit translation/rotation fragment coordinates with the original step and update.


## Cycle 4: explicit fragment translation and rotation
Candidate `5db45c8a14616f06cf1fd56be16ac8115262d590`; champion `71a74e891073ff65f11406a38a0abdff764815d0`; decision **invalid**.

**Hypothesis:** Pseudo-bond coordinates between disconnected fragments entangle intermolecular translation/rotation with intramolecular deformation. Explicit fragment centroid and quaternion rotation coordinates should improve conditioning and reduce force calls for weak complexes.
**Change:** `minimize_func` enables the existing `allow_fragments` coordinate construction. Molecular connectivity is inferred using general covalent-radius distance rules. The champion Hessian update and step policy are retained. This changes the coordinate formulation on fragmented structures, without identity-dependent rules.
**Sources:** Wang and Song, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27276946/ and https://geometric.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-it-works.html motivate explicit TRIC for intermolecular motion. This implementation retains the workspace's geodesic stepping rather than copying geomeTRIC.
**Validation:** Static syntax parsing only locally. Full remote train; energy and cost gates unchanged. If failures are localized, inspect passive bundles before bounded repair.

**Outcome:** Candidate `5db45c8a14616f06cf1fd56be16ac8115262d590`; decision **invalid**, one backend numerical error. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-4-train.json). Successful-subset relative cost about 0.901 is diagnostic only; several strongly incomplete reference energy recoveries remain.
**Passive diagnosis:** [Bundle](diagnostics/eb94be1f5de240beb03a3531fb04ab7c/5cc8806ea799725b44f205438a5b6070e39a19c6ecd441162f5ccf4095d01102.json), complete seven attempted calls/six successful, no truncation. Maximum Cartesian step grew from roughly 0.10–0.14 Angstrom to 0.233 then 0.420 Angstrom at the failed calculation; force norm increased on call 6 despite energy descent. Minimum separation stayed near 1.09 Angstrom, arguing against an atom collision. The step/SCF connection is a hypothesis, not proof.
**Interpretation:** Promising cost signal with localized numerical failure, but separate energy/basin problems in converged runs cannot be explained from retained traces.
**Next idea/control:** Bounded repair 1 of at most 3: cap predicted Cartesian atomic displacement at 0.2 Angstrom before geodesic integration. Test whether the error disappears without destroying speed; aggregate energy must still pass.


## Cycle 5: Cartesian motion cap for fragment coordinates
Candidate `ba4ffa67bc4867c0d847da7a177c2b49fb470410`; champion `71a74e891073ff65f11406a38a0abdff764815d0`; decision **invalid**.

**Hypothesis:** The cycle-4 SCF failure follows amplified Cartesian motion from mixed-unit TRIC steps. Capping the linearized physical step should stabilize that motion while retaining useful fragment conditioning.
**Change:** From preserved cycle 4, `_predict_step` scales internal step and its reported magnitude whenever the largest linearized atomic displacement exceeds 0.2 Angstrom. Applies generally, without molecule-specific checks. This is repair 1 in the fragment-TRIC sequence; no external thresholds change.
**Evidence:** Cycle 4 passive bundle and saved-result analysis above. A cap addresses observed motion growth, not the separate unexplained energy losses.
**Validation:** Static parsing; remote full train, then validation only if all training gates pass.

**Outcome:** Candidate `ba4ffa67bc4867c0d847da7a177c2b49fb470410`; decision **invalid**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-5-train.json). Same SCF failure at call 8 instead of 7. Successful-subset speed signal persists but energy worsens; these are not split scores.
**Passive diagnosis:** [Bundle](diagnostics/bd6b1e7aea3d4501bc15814a242ca683/72d8f890c319937d66d45afc1e6e7348563af1f273318676bbca6ef66d078563.json), eight attempts/seven completed, untruncated. Actual steps near 0.200 Angstrom confirm the cap works. Minimum separation remains near 1.09 Angstrom. Energy descends while force increases over the last three successful calls. Thus oversized individual steps are not a sufficient explanation.
**Interpretation:** Stop tuning the cap. A different general mechanism remains: the initial TRIC stiffness (0.05 Hartree) suppresses collective relative motion compared to the artificial-bond model, producing little energy lowering before convergence in several complexes. This could also keep fragment arrangements in problematic electronic regimes, but that link is uncertain.
**Next idea/control:** Repair 2 from preserved cycle 4, omitting the unsupported cap: lower initial fragment translation/rotation stiffness tenfold. This tests a curvature model, not convergence settings. If energy deficits and instability persist, defer this formulation.


## Cycle 6: softer fragment curvature
Candidate `2077e365ba0dd5cc51bb719b3ed82b128e5da840`; champion `71a74e891073ff65f11406a38a0abdff764815d0`; decision **keep**.

**Hypothesis:** Fragment collective motion is too stiff in the initial model, as suggested by very low reference energy recovery despite quick force convergence for weak complexes in cycles 4–5. Softer translation/rotation curvature should permit physically productive collective motion before the secant model is learned.
**Change:** From preserved cycle 4, `Internals.guess_hessian` lowers TRIC curvature from 0.05 to 0.005 Hartree. Omit the cycle-5 motion cap whose specific hypothesis was contradicted. Repair 2 of the bounded TRIC sequence.
**Validation:** Static syntax parsing only locally; full train remotely. Existing evaluation gates are unchanged. Both numerical failure and energy recovery remain open concerns.

**Training outcome:** Full training passes both gates with no errors and complete convergence. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-6-train.json). The softer model repaired the numerical failure and aggregate energy loss in this tested configuration; validation is now required. This supports model curvature as a more useful target than an individual-step cap, without proving a unique cause.

**Additional sources and directions while validation runs:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05803 (Denzel/Kästner) motivates a fundamentally different GPR optimizer with Matérn kernel and overshooting, but does not establish performance against this internal-coordinate champion. A bounded implementation could learn a local surrogate from already paid-for energies/forces and request only its proposed minimum through the supplied calculator; any such surrogate work would execute only on the remote evaluator. https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.02570 (Packwood et al.) motivates Cartesian neighborhood preconditioning as another independent coordinate formulation. No local numerical work was performed. First prioritize simpler controls of remaining intramolecular cost; cycle 6 training gains are concentrated in complexes (166 faster, 42 slower), while non-complex cases are nearly identical to the anchor.

**Final outcome:** Candidate `2077e365ba0dd5cc51bb719b3ed82b128e5da840`; **keep**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-6-train.json), [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-6-valid.json). Both complete and error-free with full convergence, aggregate energy above fixed requirements and cost below the starting champion. New champion is cycle 6.
**Interpretation:** Explicit fragment coordinates become useful with a softer collective Hessian; the bounded repair rescued the formulation. Aggregate recovery still allows individual energy regressions, so accepted improvement is exactly the fixed aggregate claim, not per-molecule dominance.
**Next idea/control:** Test a larger initial internal trust radius to reduce early step restriction for noisy starting structures. Keep the new coordinate model; evaluate generalization afresh.


## Cycle 7: larger initial trust radius
Candidate `4ee07740c283194fafaa547b093dccb5a8229337`; champion `2077e365ba0dd5cc51bb719b3ed82b128e5da840`; decision **discard**.

**Hypothesis:** The default initial internal maximum step of 0.1 restricts early corrections even when the physical model is useful. Starting at 0.2 may reduce force calls spent on these restricted steps; existing model-agreement feedback still adjusts subsequent radius.
**Change:** `minimize_func` supplies `delta0=0.2` to Sella. This is a single trust-radius initialization control on accepted cycle 6. No change to coordinates, curvature models, update or stopping.
**Validation:** Syntax parsing only locally; remote full train and eligible validation. Increased steps could change basins or cause errors, which would falsify the tested setting under fixed gates.

**Outcome:** Candidate `4ee07740c283194fafaa547b093dccb5a8229337`; **discard**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-7-train.json). Full validity and convergence but cost exceeds champion; validation skipped. No failure bundles.
**Interpretation:** Saved-result comparison shows opposite effects: mean relative-cost change about -0.024 for other structures and +0.046 for complexes. A uniform initial radius ignores the mixed displacement meaning of fragment rotation/translation versus internal bond/angle/dihedral motion. This justifies one coordinate-aware repair, not molecule-specific cases.
**Next idea/control:** Initial radius 0.2 only when the actual coordinate basis contains no translation or rotation coordinates, retaining 0.1 with those collective modes. Evaluate the whole split and retain only on unchanged gates.


## Cycle 8: coordinate-aware initial radius
Candidate `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; champion `2077e365ba0dd5cc51bb719b3ed82b128e5da840`; decision **keep**.

**Hypothesis:** Cycle 7's opposite cost effects reflect coordinate scaling. Bond/angle/dihedral steps can begin at 0.2, while explicit collective motion benefits from the champion radius 0.1.
**Change:** `minimize_func` sets the initial radius to 0.2 only if the constructed basis has no translation and no rotation coordinates. This is a physical coordinate-representation rule applying to arbitrary molecules, not an identity or dataset-category rule. Repair 1 of the larger-radius idea.
**Evidence:** Cycle 7 complete training and saved comparisons. No numerical exceptions or nonconvergence traces exist; this repair addresses the observed cost interaction.
**Validation:** Local syntax parsing; full remote train followed by eligible validation.

**Outcome:** Candidate `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; **keep**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-8-train.json), [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-8-valid.json). Complete, valid, error-free with all molecules converged. Both cost gates passed against cycle 6.
**Interpretation:** Coordinate-aware initialization rescued the aggregate cost failure of a uniform larger radius, consistent with different physical meaning of collective and bonded coordinate steps. This does not establish an optimal radius.
**Next idea/control:** Substantial optimizer replacement: Cartesian quasi-Newton minimization initialized by the accepted molecular model Hessian. This tests whether better defined Cartesian secants can offset loss of geodesic coordinate stepping.


## Cycle 9: model-preconditioned Cartesian optimizer
Candidate `78d9ff9546cb1c0fba52bf18a992bd333dde5fe4`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **discard**.

**Hypothesis:** The useful chemical conditioning of internal coordinates can be retained through a Cartesian model Hessian, while Cartesian secants avoid nonlinear gradient transport and inconsistent tangent spaces. A complete replacement of the minimization loop tests whether that benefit outweighs losing geodesic steps.
**Change:** `_cartesian_model_hessian` maps the champion's primitive model by J-transpose H J and eliminates dummy coordinates by a Schur complement; a positive floor stabilizes null modes. `minimize_func` is replaced with a Cartesian damped-BFGS trust algorithm, learning from uphill trials and retrying from the accepted point. Maximum atomic motion initializes at 0.15 Angstrom and changes according to actual/predicted energy reduction. All actual calls are counted and the exact last evaluated array is returned even if that trial was rejected. The supplied internal-coordinate utilities are retained as model-building code, with no numerical calls outside the supplied calculator.
**Sources:** Mones, Ortner and Csanyi (2018), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-32105-x , particularly its positive internal-derivative construction, motivates a Cartesian preconditioner. This implementation uses the approved workspace's existing heuristic curvatures, not a new force-field energy calculator. Damped Cartesian updates follow the previously cited SciPy/Nocedal strategy; the unsuccessful internal-coordinate variant in cycle 2 does not establish its behavior in Cartesian space.
**Validation:** Local syntax parsing only. All optimizer execution is remote, full training first. This is an independent formulation; failures must be classified before any bounded repair.

**Outcome:** Candidate `78d9ff9546cb1c0fba52bf18a992bd333dde5fe4`; **discard**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-9-train.json). Valid aggregate energy, no internal errors, but roughly twice reference cost, five call-limit outcomes, and only 12 molecules faster than champion.
**Passive diagnosis:** [Manifest](diagnostics/739ced1b34f540fd994e7274440703a4/manifest.json). Examined [flexible-molecule bundle](diagnostics/739ced1b34f540fd994e7274440703a4/5f51778d1884594990060793136dcb01c06f424332ee8bd5d7532854eae0dec7.json) and [complex bundle](diagnostics/739ced1b34f540fd994e7274440703a4/2b75ba9beb2638d59c9141dedfe0ccfb52a224c56f56ec6c283d363b4aaaa080.json). Each retains all 200 scalar records but only eight final frames. Just 7 and 10 uphill transitions, respectively; late iterations continue smooth energy lowering with substantial motion. This argues against repeated rejection as the dominant issue and points toward slow curvature learning along soft modes.
**Interpretation:** Initial Cartesian preconditioning alone fails to retain the speed of moving internal coordinates in this formulation. A recomputed preconditioner with limited-memory corrections might avoid stale geometric curvature, as discussed by Mones et al.; the present evidence does not test that method. No localized numerical repair is justified for the broad slowdown.
**Next idea/control:** Restore champion. Test one-time scalar calibration of the initial internal Hessian from its first secant, preserving its anisotropic chemical structure.


## Cycle 10: first-secant model scale calibration
Candidate `6742314709fc7d31ea6585b9ceb2a28de63e4fca`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **non_generalizable**.

**Hypothesis:** The heuristic initial molecular Hessian can have a good anisotropic shape but the wrong overall stiffness for xTB. Its first transported secant provides a free directional calibration; scaling the whole model once before the usual update may reduce later curvature-learning calls.
**Change:** `ApproximateHessian` marks explicit starting matrices for a one-time fit. On the first vector update, scale by observed/model directional curvature, clipped to [0.5, 2], when both curvatures are positive. Then apply the existing TS-BFGS update. No additional force evaluations or altered coordinates/stopping. The model's relative stiffnesses are preserved.
**Source:** The previously read SciPy BFGS documentation describes automatic initial scaling from secant information; this adapts that principle to an anisotropic chemical model rather than an identity matrix. It is a hypothesis because the first direction may not represent other modes.
**Validation:** Static syntax parsing only; all measurements through full remote training and eligible validation. A cost or energy failure rejects this specific calibration.

**Next-source exploration while validation runs:** https://doi.org/10.3390/math14101750 reviews modified secants using theta = 6(f_old-f_new)+3(g_old+g_new).s; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S037704270600344X discusses higher-order curvature information from function values. A possible next test would use the already observed energy change to correct the directional secant, with a bounded correction and endpoint geodesic directional derivatives. This is distinct from the scalar initialization fit; neither idea is assumed useful without evaluation. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927025617301131 motivates on-the-fly internal force-constant fitting as another related direction.

**Outcome:** Candidate `6742314709fc7d31ea6585b9ceb2a28de63e4fca`; **non_generalizable**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-10-train.json), [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-10-valid.json). Both energy valid and error-free; the small training cost gain reverses on validation.
**Interpretation:** One early secant does not give a reliably generalizable scalar calibration. No failure traces exist because all molecules converged. Future fitting should distinguish mode classes or accumulate multiple independent directions, rather than tune this scalar from validation.
**Next idea/control:** Restore cycle 8. Test bounded energy-informed secants, using the cubic-Hermite residual between actual energy change and endpoint directional gradients.


## Cycle 11: energy-informed geodesic secants
Candidate `bd0cf6def371fb4404b735560d0cd7ff7e7c9328`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **discard**.

**Hypothesis:** Ordinary secants estimate average directional curvature, but the next step needs endpoint curvature. The measured energy change plus endpoint gradients defines a cubic-Hermite residual that can improve that estimate without additional force calls.
**Change:** `PES.kick` forms theta = 3(g_old.s_initial + g_new.s_final)-6 delta_energy and adds theta*s_final/||s_final||^2 to the transported gradient difference before TS-BFGS. The correction is clipped to half the magnitude of directional secant curvature; tiny residuals/steps are ignored for numerical stability. Geodesic endpoint tangents replace a single straight displacement, so this is a tested adaptation rather than an assertion that Euclidean convergence proofs apply unchanged.
**Sources:** https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S037704270600344X and https://doi.org/10.3390/math14101750 motivate energy-augmented secants. Search excerpts exposed the formula; fetching the latter full text returned HTTP 429. The scalar formula also follows directly by differentiating cubic Hermite interpolation of energy along a step.
**Validation:** Local syntax parsing only. Remote full training, then validation if eligible. No change in force-call accounting, energy requirements or stopping criteria.

**Outcome:** Candidate `bd0cf6def371fb4404b735560d0cd7ff7e7c9328`; **discard**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-11-train.json). All converged/error-free and energy valid, but cost worsened; 113 faster and 174 slower than champion. No passive failure traces.
**Interpretation:** The bounded Hermite correction does not improve this transported internal model overall. Endpoint energy consistency along a curve is not automatically the right vector secant correction in a redundant metric; the derivation needs further care before retuning.
**Next idea/control:** Restore champion and test faster trust growth only after model agreement, distinguishing learned confidence from cycle 7's unconditional initial radius increase.


## Cycle 12: faster trust growth after model agreement
Candidate `26db3d2e73817d6a305d047a511068eb590b2dea`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **invalid**.

**Hypothesis:** Once actual/predicted energy change agrees, 15% trust growth may waste force calls on unnecessarily restricted steps. Growing by 50% only under the existing agreement condition should accelerate learned, reliable directions without enlarging the uncertain initial collective step.
**Change:** `minimize_func` sets `sigma_inc=1.5`; retain the champion's coordinate-aware initial radius, shrink policy, Hessian model/update, and agreement window. This is a single trust-growth control, distinct from rejected uniform initialization in cycle 7.
**Evidence/source:** Cycles 7–8 demonstrate that initial step confidence differs by coordinate type; https://geometric.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-it-works.html motivates trust growth based on model agreement. No claim that 1.5 is optimal.
**Validation:** Static parsing only locally, full training remotely and validation if eligible.

**Outcome:** Candidate `26db3d2e73817d6a305d047a511068eb590b2dea`; **invalid**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-12-train.json). One geometry-integration exception. Successful-subset cost is worse than champion, with 65 faster versus 165 slower cases; it is not a split score.
**Passive diagnosis:** [Bundle](diagnostics/772baab523654021a1d05de0c5d1faf4/797b7be28b87db4230696a79622eaf0c455821f73e7b16acb8dd6a6cb45939b0.json) retains all 19 scalar records and eight final frames. Several late steps have multi-Bohr displacement and very large force/energy excursions before the ODE iteration guard raises. Faster growth overwhelms the permissive existing contraction policy in this case.
**Interpretation:** This growth-only setting is not promising enough to keep pursuing: both stability and cost worsen, beyond the single error. A future redesigned trust policy would need balanced contraction, but current evidence does not justify a parameter sequence here. No deferred implementation added for this one-parameter rejection.
**Next idea/control:** Revisit `cartesian-model` with its specifically proposed dynamic positive preconditioner plus L-BFGS, guided by cycle 9's smooth but slow soft-mode progress and Mones et al.'s dynamic construction.


## Cycle 13: moving Cartesian molecular preconditioner
Candidate `925a1daa8df2a6d0d3321d479633b9b92bf8075a`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **discard**.

**Hypothesis:** Cycle 9's smooth but slow convergence reflects stale geometric curvature in its initial-only Cartesian model. Rebuilding the positive model at each accepted geometry and applying limited-memory secant corrections should follow changing bond/angle directions more effectively.
**Change:** Revisit preserved cycle 9. `_cartesian_model_inverse` rebuilds and inverts the positive model at each accepted geometry. The Cartesian loop uses 16-pair L-BFGS with that current metric; positive-curvature accepted pairs are retained, uphill trials shrink the radius and retry from the accepted point. The same initial/max Cartesian radius is retained from cycle 9. The quadratic prediction along an L-BFGS direction uses its implicit inverse relation, avoiding a separate approximate Hessian. All model work runs only remotely and uses geometry/heuristic stiffness, not a second force calculator.
**Evidence/source:** Cycle 9 passive bundles show continuing slow descent rather than repeated rejection. Mones et al., https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-32105-x , motivate a recomputed geometric preconditioner in Cartesian optimization. This is repair 1 of the Cartesian-model formulation, with a specific mechanism rather than step-cap tuning.
**Validation:** Static syntax parsing only locally. Full remote train and eligible validation; exceptions and energy/cost gates unchanged.

**Outcome:** Candidate `925a1daa8df2a6d0d3321d479633b9b92bf8075a`; **discard**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-13-train.json). Energy valid/no internal errors, but cost worsens relative to both champion and cycle 9. Seven force-call-limit receipts; each has all 200 attempted/completed calls and truncated frame history. No optimizer-error repair is indicated.
**Interpretation:** Recomputed Cartesian model plus 16-pair L-BFGS does not rescue this formulation. The two tested variants do not establish a general impossibility for Cartesian preconditioning, but there is no current evidence-backed repair direction. Close this sequence without spending its remaining repair allowance.
**Next idea/control:** Restore champion and remove overall rigid-body modes from TRIC's free subspace. Relative fragment translation/rotation remains free; only global energy-invariant motions are constrained.


## Cycle 14: remove global rigid modes from fragment coordinates
Candidate `3e8172bb089896212bca0289f5086340b5d2b1db`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **discard**.

**Hypothesis:** Explicit fragment coordinates span overall translation and rotation as well as energy-changing relative motion. Mixed-coordinate preconditioning may send part of a step into these null directions. Projecting them out should spend more of the trust radius on geometry changes that can lower energy.
**Change:** `InternalPES.__init__` adds overall real-atom translation and rotational tangent constraints when collective coordinates exist. Relative fragment motion stays free. The existing constraint machinery projects free directions and maintains the translation gauge; existing `ignore_rotation=True` uses a rotational tangent gauge rather than forcing finite orientation residuals. No physical internal coordinate is fixed and no evaluator threshold changes.
**Sources/context:** TRIC's full 3N span is described at https://geometric.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-it-works.html . The approved workspace's Cartesian PES already projects global rigid modes; this tests the same symmetry principle for TRIC.
**Validation:** Static parsing only locally. Full remote train and eligible validation. Changes to numerical conditioning or constrained geodesic transport may hurt performance; fixed gates decide.

**Outcome:** Candidate `3e8172bb089896212bca0289f5086340b5d2b1db`; **discard**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-14-train.json). Full convergence, energy validity and no errors, but cost exceeds champion. No failure/nonconvergence bundles exist.
**Interpretation:** Removing global gauge directions is mathematically legitimate but does not improve this implementation's force-call efficiency. Added constrained transport may offset any reduction of null motion. No diagnosed repair or concrete follow-up justifies retaining this edit in the active backlog.
**Next idea/control:** Revisit `model-scale-calibration` with regularized fitting of physical coordinate blocks over six early secants, then ordinary TS-BFGS. Freysoldt (2017), https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927025617301131 , describes fitting a small number of internal force constants on the fly from observed force changes; its solid-state results motivate a molecular experiment, not an assumed improvement.


## Cycle 15: regularized physical-block Hessian calibration
Candidate `103f2fdfee3ef9f388cd082b4a7c4a2eefb59b6d`; champion `46ea0b05db756c6f9842a66e5ce3cf27a848c764`; decision **keep**.

**Hypothesis:** Cycle 10's one-direction global scaling can misrepresent other modes. A small regularized fit of bond, angle, torsion and collective stiffness over six early secants should provide a more representative initial model while retaining physical anisotropy.
**Change:** `InternalPES.__init__` keeps projected positive model blocks by coordinate type. A new `_update_H` accumulates normalized secant normal equations with a prior toward unit scales; fitted scales stay within [0.5,2]. It reconstructs the starting model and replays all observed TS-BFGS updates for the first six secants, then returns to ordinary updates. No new force calls, no external metadata or learned molecule identities. This is repair 1 of the model-calibration idea after cycle 10's validation cost failure.
**Source:** Freysoldt (2017), https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927025617301131 , motivates fitting a low-dimensional physical Hessian model from force changes. Here the classes are generic coordinate types rather than element/bond subclasses, and fitting is limited to an early window. Transported secants from different geometries remain an approximation; the evaluation tests its usefulness.
**Validation:** Local syntax parsing only; full train remotely, validation only after both gates pass.

**Outcome:** Candidate `103f2fdfee3ef9f388cd082b4a7c4a2eefb59b6d`; **keep**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-15-train.json), [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-15-valid.json). Complete, error-free, fully converged and energy-valid on both splits; both cost gates pass against cycle 8.
**Interpretation:** Physical-block fitting over several directions rescues the failed scalar calibration in this configuration. Training gains occur in both complexes and other structures, supporting broader utility than a single subgroup. Validation gain is smaller but clears the unchanged gate.
**Next idea/control:** Safeguarded GDIIS after early curvature fitting, using at most five recent nearby geometries and a bounded descent direction. https://manual.q-chem.com/5.3/A1.S7.html gives the error-vector interpolation formula and notes that GDIIS is not consistently superior to standard steps; the experiment must establish value here.


## Cycle 16: safeguarded geometry DIIS
Candidate `ac78a1e098f2e430c8536ae6797d1d52a9d9f79e`; champion `103f2fdfee3ef9f388cd082b4a7c4a2eefb59b6d`; decision **non_generalizable**.

**Hypothesis:** Once the early physical Hessian fit settles, recent geometries and gradients contain information about correlated errors that a single quasi-Newton direction misses. GDIIS may accelerate remaining local relaxation without new force evaluations.
**Change:** `Sella._predict_step` offers the ordinary step to `_gdiis_step`. The latter keeps up to five nearby history points, clears history on energy increase or coordinate-system reset, and starts after six steps. It minimizes the norm of affine-combined preconditioned gradient errors in the current free subspace, then constructs the standard geometry-plus-Newton-correction proposal. Regularization, coefficient L1 bound, descent requirement, existing trust bound and a 1.5-times ordinary-step norm limit guard extrapolation; otherwise use the champion step. Inequality-constrained paths retain ordinary steps. All proposals still use the original geodesic update, real calculator and stopping callback.
**Source:** https://manual.q-chem.com/5.3/A1.S7.html , equations A.33–A.41; its caveat about inconsistent speed benefit motivates explicit testing. The method uses current-Hessian error vectors and wrapped primitive coordinate differences; curvature of the redundant chart remains an uncertainty.
**Validation:** Static parsing only locally. Full training remotely, then eligible validation.

**Outcome:** Candidate `ac78a1e098f2e430c8536ae6797d1d52a9d9f79e`; **non_generalizable**. [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-16-train.json), [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-16-valid.json). Training passes cost/energy with one call-limit trajectory. Validation reduces cost but fails aggregate energy despite all molecules converging and no internal errors.
**Passive diagnosis:** [Training bundle](diagnostics/20b002e9da7c4688ba00deab392d6f3d/3d75e77cdf4dff4d02015198c07186930183a19ae33914f3241bf79075b8eaf5.json) contains all 200 scalar records and eight final frames. It shows extended descent through large energy changes and several excursions, not a fixed-position convergence loop. Validation has no failure bundles; its dominant relative-energy loss is a changed basin, so its exact path is unavailable.
**Interpretation:** Local DIIS speed signal is promising on both splits, but monotone energy/gradient history alone does not ensure a locally quadratic region. Early extrapolation remains a plausible explanation, not proven for the converged validation cases.
**Next idea/control:** Repair 1: require the ordinary Newton step to use less than half the current trust radius and the previous actual/predicted energy ratio to be in the existing good-agreement window. This tests a general local-model-confidence criterion, never a molecular identity.

Candidate `7d2a6e5070b7bf92745bad3088a033d53ee90368`; champion `103f2fdfee3ef9f388cd082b4a7c4a2eefb59b6d`; decision **discard**.

## Cycle 19: low-dimensional gradient-enhanced surrogate steps
Candidate `a41daef1b418e964afce5729263cf10c4d5fdd98`; champion `103f2fdfee3ef9f388cd082b4a7c4a2eefb59b6d`; decision **invalid**.

**Hypothesis:** A nonlinear surrogate can combine recent energies and gradients more usefully than linear DIIS, while a physical quadratic prior prevents aimless extrapolation with sparse data.
**Change:** New `Sella._surrogate_step` builds a rank-at-most-five motion subspace from the ordinary step and up to five nearby geometry differences. The current Hessian whitens this subspace; a squared-exponential GP fits energy and gradient residuals around its quadratic prior. Analytic covariance derivatives support at most twelve surrogate-only BFGS microiterations remotely. The actual force calculator remains outside these microiterations. Current energy/gradient are enforced exactly by subtracting fitted origin errors. Proposals require descent, existing trust size, at most 1.5 times ordinary norm, better surrogate energy and bounded posterior uncertainty; otherwise use the ordinary step. History resets on energy increase or coordinate reset and activates only after six physical-model secants. No identity-based choices or convergence changes.
**Source:** Raggi et al., https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.0c00257 and its public preprint abstract/supporting file https://s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/itempdf74155353254prod/11950491/Restricted-Variance_Molecular_Geometry_Optimization_Based_on_Gradient-Enhanced_Kriging_v3.pdf motivate physical-curvature length scales and uncertainty restriction. This compact quadratic-mean, subspace implementation is an independent experiment, not a reproduction of their full method. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378918/ supports investigating internal-coordinate representations.
**Uncertainty/control:** Primitive-coordinate history derivatives approximate a common local chart; projection can omit relevant transverse variation. Remote costs may expose these limits. Comparison is against cycle 15 with unchanged full-split gates; all local validation is static parsing only.

**Static follow-up while pending:** Review identified an interface mistake: `PES` exposes `get_HL_projected(basis)`, not `get_HL()`. The candidate remains unchanged until the remote decision resolves; any correction will be a new committed cycle.

**Outcome:** [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-19-train.json) completes with 449 identical missing-accessor exceptions. The remaining 20 terminate before the surrogate activates. No numerical conclusion about the GP step is justified.
**Interpretation:** This is an implementation error, corroborating the static review. Failure details identify the exact call; the existing `get_HL_projected(basis)` implements the desired projected Lagrangian Hessian directly.
**Next idea/control:** Repair 1 changes only that accessor, with identical GP design and complete remote gates. Preserve the initial implementation and error evidence.

**Cycle 19 passive evidence:** [Complete seven-call bundle](diagnostics/21dc2de3b99448bfaf628eaf2c444b57/57b4036fb8369aec0038235cad12ddca868de0b5eb1cd834e13b1f96a2025238.json) confirms the missing accessor before surrogate construction; frames and scalar history are untruncated.

## Cycle 20: repair the surrogate Hessian interface
Candidate `c94c425f8c57f8fddbe81012e20febe7625547a5`; champion `103f2fdfee3ef9f388cd082b4a7c4a2eefb59b6d`; decision **keep**.

**Hypothesis:** The nonlinear surrogate idea in cycle 19 is scientifically untested because an accessor error stops activation. Correcting that call will expose its actual behavior.
**Change:** Starting from the preserved cycle 19 source, replace the unavailable full-Hessian accessor/projection with `self.pes.get_HL_projected(basis).asarray()`. No other numerical choices change. Repair 1 of `subspace-gp`.
**Validation:** Static parsing and inspection of the existing projected accessor. Numerical measurements only through full remote training and eligible validation.

**Further source review while pending:** The full preprint was accessible at https://chemrxiv.org/engage/api-gateway/chemrxiv/assets/orp/resource/item/60c74a579abda25a9cf8ce2c/original/restricted-variance-molecular-geometry-optimization-based-on-gradient-enhanced-kriging.pdf . Its variance expression includes an empirical residual scale, and its microiterations enforce uncertainty limits during optimization. Cycle 20 instead uses fixed normalized covariance amplitude and rejects an over-uncertain endpoint. These are material implementation differences, not established faults; revisit only if the measured results justify a targeted repair. The paper also uses a Matérn kernel and a constant trend, whereas this experiment tests a squared-exponential residual around the champion quadratic model.

**Outcome:** [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-20-train.json) and [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-20-valid.json) pass all unchanged gates, with full convergence and no errors. The corrected GP becomes champion. Both requests included long pending intervals; service wall duration is higher, while the objective's force-call cost improves. The evidence does not isolate the cause of wall-time differences.
**Interpretation:** Nonlinear energy/gradient interpolation with a quadratic prior succeeds where linear GDIIS did not generalize in energy. Training has 158 faster and 65 slower cases, with average gains in both complexes and other structures. Some largest cost regressions reach lower energy, while others reach effectively the same endpoint more slowly. No failure bundles exist for completed converged runs, so internal surrogate decisions remain untraced.
**Next idea/control:** Use empirical GP residual amplitude in the posterior uncertainty test, as motivated by the preprint variance equation. This isolates confidence calibration, leaving the posterior mean, microiterations and force-call contract unchanged. It may reject poorly fit nonlinear history and permit well fit steps; compare directly against this new champion.


## Cycle 21: calibrate GP uncertainty from observed residuals
Candidate `26f93c15025242f7e2c8ff9501541b26cf5be9a2`; champion `c94c425f8c57f8fddbe81012e20febe7625547a5`; decision **non_generalizable**.

**Hypothesis:** Fixed unit covariance amplitude ignores how well the physical quadratic prior fits the actual history. Estimating the residual amplitude can make the uncertainty acceptance test more informative and reduce unproductive proposals without suppressing well learned motion.
**Change:** In `Sella._surrogate_step`, multiply the normalized posterior variance by `max(target.T @ Kinv @ target / observation_count, 1e-12)`. The fitted mean, kernel length scale, candidate, trust bound and all other safeguards are unchanged. This adapts the residual-scale factor in equation 14 of the Raggi et al. preprint linked in cycle 20; it is a general fit statistic, not a molecular identity.
**Validation:** Static parsing only locally. Full training remotely, followed by validation only if it improves over cycle 20 and remains energy-valid. Because this statistic includes all retained observations, distant history might make it too conservative; that is a falsifiable limitation of this experiment.

**Outcome:** [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-21-train.json) passes both gates; [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-21-valid.json) passes energy but loses cost against cycle 20. All cases converge with no errors and no retained failure bundles.
**Interpretation:** Training improvement is concentrated: 32 cases improve, 41 worsen, 396 are unchanged, with large gains on several previous slowdowns. The validation cost loss means this global residual-scale statistic is not an improvement in the tested setting. No trace identifies which GP acceptance decisions caused it; another confidence-threshold adjustment is not justified.
**Next idea/control:** Independently compare the covariance kernel on the restored champion. Denzel and Kästner https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.05803 , section II.A, attribute their Matérn advantage to less extrapolation oscillation. Their Cartesian setting differs from this subspace method. Match zero-distance gradient covariance to avoid an arbitrary local-stiffness change, and let full evaluation decide.


## Cycle 22: Matérn covariance for the compact surrogate
Candidate `da1ff4766b6bc2974934d5c284ff1ddf3b0a6a47`; champion `c94c425f8c57f8fddbe81012e20febe7625547a5`; decision **non_generalizable**.

**Hypothesis:** The squared-exponential residual model can oscillate during nearby extrapolation. A Matérn 5/2 kernel may yield more useful nonlinear corrections while retaining the accepted physical prior and small motion subspace.
**Change:** Replace only covariance values and analytic first/mixed derivatives in `Sella._surrogate_step`. With r the whitened distance, use k=(1+a r+a²r²/3)exp(-a r), a²=3/4. This matches the prior kernel's value and gradient covariance at zero separation. The mixed derivative is c I - b ddᵀ, c=(a²/3)(1+a r)exp(-a r), b=(a⁴/3)exp(-a r), with no division by r at coincident points. All optimizer, history and uncertainty safeguards remain as in champion cycle 20; rejected empirical amplitude is absent.
**Source/control:** https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.05803 , equations 2–3 and section II.A, report a Matérn advantage for Cartesian GP optimization. This tests whether that kernel-shape mechanism transfers to an internal motion subspace; its usefulness here is not assumed.
**Validation:** Static syntax parsing and manual derivative/shape review only locally. Complete remote training and eligible validation under unchanged gates.

**Outcome:** [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-22-train.json) passes cost and energy; [validation](evaluation_results/cycle-22-valid.json) passes energy but fails cost. All cases converge without internal errors, so there are no passive failure trajectories.
**Interpretation:** The Matérn gain is not generalizable in this configuration. Training improves on 74 cases and worsens on 78; average gain is concentrated in complexes, with a small average loss elsewhere. Published Cartesian results do not transfer automatically to this projected quadratic-residual model. A kernel-range sweep is not justified by the available endpoint evidence.
**Next idea/control:** Restore the accepted squared-exponential model and test iterative internal-to-Cartesian conversion only for GP-selected steps. The surrogate predicts an internal coordinate target; closer realization of that target may improve the model/trajectory agreement. https://geometric.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-it-works.html describes the iterative residual-correction approach. The existing fallback to geodesic integration provides a bounded implementation test; coordinate feasibility and gradient transport remain uncertainties. The alternative initial-Hessian direction reviewed from Lindh/Bakken-Helgaker remains a later independent control, not combined here.


## Cycle 23: iterative realization of surrogate coordinate targets
Candidate `058d5d6234243b38593b40b86b207dd25c864da4`; champion `c94c425f8c57f8fddbe81012e20febe7625547a5`; decision **non_generalizable**.

**Hypothesis:** GP proposals minimize a model expressed in internal-coordinate differences, while the geodesic converter interprets them as initial tangent vectors. Trying to realize the predicted target directly may improve force-call efficiency by reducing that discrepancy.
**Change:** `Sella._predict_step` resets the iterative-conversion flag for each new step; `_surrogate_step` enables it only when a GP proposal passes all existing acceptance checks. `InternalPES._set_x_iterative` is the pre-existing bounded Newton residual correction, with restoration and geodesic fallback for infeasible, divergent or poorly converged coordinate targets. Ordinary steps retain the accepted geodesic path. No calculator, stopping criteria or call-count changes.

This is not a reproduction of geomeTRIC. The target may be infeasible in redundant coordinates, and the existing gradient transport may differ from geodesic transport; these are tested uncertainties rather than assumed improvements.

**Interpretation:** Matching surrogate coordinate targets with this existing converter does not improve validation efficiency. Training has 40 faster, 38 slower and 391 unchanged cases, with positive average gains in both broad groups. Endpoint evidence cannot distinguish changed basin paths from altered curvature learning. The converter's approximate gradient transport is another uncertainty, so its geometric target consistency alone does not establish a superior optimizer.
**Next idea/control:** Restore the champion and test a Lindh-style initial Hessian with distance-product angle/torsion stiffness. Keep the accepted six-secant physical-block calibration and GP model. ## Cycle 24: distance-product initial curvature model
Candidate `17ffe8074faada78ba31233300bec89024415bf2`; champion `c94c425f8c57f8fddbe81012e20febe7625547a5`; decision **discard**.

**Hypothesis:** An initial Hessian whose angle/torsion stiffness decays with all participating bond distances can better model soft or stretched internal modes before early secant fitting, reducing force calls before and after GP activation.
**Change:** Add `Internals._lindh_rho` and use positive distance-product force constants in `guess_hessian` for real-atom bonds, angles and torsions. Nominal constants are 0.45, 0.15 and 0.005 in atomic units. Pair decay distinguishes first-period pairs from heavier pairs using published alpha values, but uses sums of the existing covalent radii as reference distances to cover the full element range; exponent clipping guards arithmetic extremes. This is explicitly a covalent-radius adaptation, not the original period-distance table. Dummy-coordinate models and collective translation/rotation curvature remain unchanged. The accepted physical-block calibration, GP and trust method are unchanged.
**Source:** Lindh's model summarized in Bakken and Helgaker, https://trygvehelgaker.no/Publications/JChemPhys_117_09160_2002.pdf , equations 40–41 and Table I. Its distance-product construction motivates the experiment; generalization and interaction with online calibration are open questions.
**Validation:** Static parsing and geometry/units review only locally. Full remote training and eligible validation under unchanged gates. No preliminary force or optimizer calculations.

**Outcome:** [Training](evaluation_results/cycle-24-train.json) is complete, fully converged, error-free and energy-valid, but fails cost. Validation skipped. No failure bundles are retained for these converged runs.
**Interpretation:** There are 157 faster and 218 slower cases; average cost worsens in both broad groups. Some large slowdowns reach substantially lower energies, but others reach nearly the same endpoint. The failure is broad, so no geometric step-cap repair is indicated.
**Next idea/control:** One bounded model-parameter follow-up: restore the published first-three-period reference distances, which were paired with the nominal force constants. The covalent-radius substitution changes relative stiffness for heteroatom bonds and their angle/torsion products. This is a source-based hypothesis, not a cause proven by the endpoint evidence. The source table is available in extracted PDF text; screenshot rendering was unavailable in the web tool. Retain covalent radii only as an explicit extension for heavier elements, outside the published table. Reassess this model after that control rather than tuning its force constants.

The latter expression cancels the potentially singular SR1 denominator before arithmetic. Both components satisfy the same single secant, so the blend does too; it can represent negative curvature. ## Cycle 41: residual-alignment rank-one curvature blend
Candidate `f56535e29a1c699bb1a1ea59ae6f57f047fda88e`; champion `b1714c735090ec636c9accf8a541bd5559bd8577`; decision **keep**.

**Hypothesis:** When the secant residual aligns well with the step, a rank-one correction may recover useful signed curvature more directly than native TS-BFGS. Smoothly retaining TS-BFGS near orthogonality may avoid SR1 instability while improving convergence in poorly modeled directions.
**Change:** In `update_H`'s TS-BFGS branch, single-pair updates blend the native correction with SR1 using squared residual/step cosine. Implement the weighted rank-one term as c*(norm(e)/norm(s))*outer(e_hat,e_hat), avoiding division by e.s. Degenerate step/residual and multi-pair paths remain native. The model fit and replay use the same update convention; coordinate stepping, trust control, GP and public contract remain accepted behavior.
**Source/derivation:** https://trygvehelgaker.no/Publications/JChemPhys_117_09160_2002.pdf equations 42–47 motivate residual-alignment blending. This adaptation blends with TS-BFGS rather than published ordinary BFGS. For nondegenerate single secants both corrections map s to e, and their weights sum to one, so the blended update retains the secant equation and symmetry. Negative curvature is allowed and handled by the existing ordinary-step spectral convention.
**Uncertainty/control:** Better local curvature need not yield better trajectories; signed modes and imperfect geodesic secants may undermine the rank-one contribution. Test this one update idea from cycle 32, without rejected GP/transport/calibration variants.
**Validation:** Syntax, symbolic dimensions, zero/orthogonal limits and unchanged entry-point AST review only locally. Remote full training and eligible validation supply all measurements.

**Independent bound-model lead while pending:** Static inspection finds `MaxInternalStep` searches only the scalar-shifted Newton path until the largest weighted internal step hits its bound. It does not minimize the quadratic over all directions allowed by that box intersected with the free tangent space. An independent candidate could refine only boundary-active steps via a convex quadratic solve in the free-space coordinates, keeping the native absolute-eigenvalue Hessian, existing component bounds and ordinary step as feasible warm start. Accept only finite feasible proposals with lower quadratic model; the ordinary path remains fallback. Source https://cerfacs.fr/algor/reports/2007/TR_PA_07_42.pdf section 2 motivates box-shaped model minimization; no multilevel algorithm is proposed here. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/optimize.minimize-slsqp.html documents a possible bounded-iteration solver with analytic gradients and linear constraints. This changes step selection, not curvature fitting or the evaluation gates. Increased inner runtime and more aggressive boundary directions are uncertainties. A separate signed-spectrum trust-region lead was also reviewed at https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/0904038 ; the first box probe should retain accepted positive curvature to isolate the constrained-search mechanism.

**Training:** [Complete evidence](evaluation_results/cycle-41-train.json) passes cost and energy with all 469 cases converged and no errors. The residual-alignment curvature blend has a clear aggregate training advantage; validation remains necessary.

**Training diagnosis:** Compared with cycle 32, 125 cases are faster, 85 slower and 259 unchanged. Both broad groups improve, with a larger mean gain among molecular complexes. All cases converge and failure details are empty; this supports testing generalization but supplies no internal update trace.
**Box-model derivation for a future independent candidate:** In the free basis P^T used by `MaxInternalStep`, the accepted positive quadratic has g, V and positive L from its native QN stepper. With t=V sqrt(scale/L), z=t y and scale=max(z0^T H z0,1e-8), the model divided by scale is (t^T g/scale)^T y + 0.5 y^T y. Bounds become -delta-w*scons <= diag(w) P^T t y <= delta-w*scons. Thus a linear-constrained solve can use an identity Hessian without changing the physical model. Warm start y0=diag(sqrt(L/scale)) V^T z0. Skip nonpositive numerical eigenvalues rather than changing them. Retain native interior steps; on the boundary use bounded SLSQP iterations with analytic derivatives and accept only finite, feasible, lower-model proposals. Derivation only; no implementation or local execution while cycle 41 is pending.

**Outcome:** [Validation](evaluation_results/cycle-41-valid.json) passes both cost and energy, with all 465 cases converged and no errors. The decision writer keeps cycle 41 as the new champion. Relative cost is about 16.5% below the fixed training reference and 13.5% below the validation reference.
**Interpretation:** Smooth residual-alignment rank-one curvature improves both full splits under unchanged gates. This supports the tested blend, not unrestricted SR1 or alternative weighting. The effect on individual trajectories still varies and no successful-run internal traces exist.
**Next idea/control:** Use accepted cycle 41 as the anchor for the independent box-constrained quadratic refinement derived above. Retain its curvature model and bounds, and change only how boundary-active ordinary steps are selected.

## Cycle 44: common-chart historical gradients for the GP
Candidate `25ee3d6b59bf3db31e30c6edada6d3c6df1bc5b7`; champion `f56535e29a1c699bb1a1ea59ae6f57f047fda88e`; decision **discard**.

The chain-rule formula is derived under cycle 43. At the current point the map is identity on the tangent space; historical-basis rotations cancel between V and the inverse overlap. This is chart differentiation rather than isometric parallel transport.

Therefore cycle 44's derivative derivation alone does not justify enabling that old converter. A genuine chart-realization follow-up would require solving U_current^T(q_new-q_current)=z and defining consistent curvature secants; this remains a separate derivation, not an automatic combination with a rejected implementation.

A coupled Gaussian prior can preserve the accepted global-scale penalty while regularizing contrasts: for bond-scale vector w and mean m, penalty=lambda[(m-1)^2+||w-m*1||^2], giving precision lambda[I-11^T/k+11^T/k^2] and right-hand side precision*1. The eigenvalues are lambda on contrasts and lambda/k on the common direction, so the prior is positive definite and reduces exactly to the accepted scalar prior at k=1. Keep lambda=0.25, the accepted six-secant fit and physical clipping unchanged. This supplies a concrete shared-versus-contrast model for `element-pair-calibration`, rather than tuning a validation threshold. It does not prove that cycle 39's regression was caused by the prior; a normal full-split evaluation would test that explanation. No implementation or local numerical test has been run for it.

A consistent alternative is to integrate an entire initial orthonormal nonredundant frame U along the same geodesic. With Cartesian velocity v, D(v)=dB/dx applied to v, and C initially B0^+ U, use x'=v, v'=-B(x)^+ D(v)v, C'=-B(x)^+ D(v)C. Then F=B_end C_end is the parallel image of U; in exact arithmetic F^T F=I. The initial quadratic prediction must also use the saved initial U, rather than projecting old data with the endpoint tangent basis. Before the new secant update, transport H through F, then clear the per-step transport state. ## Cycle 51: weighted primitive-coordinate gradient regression
Candidate `ce3fd31b6acd71ca50217e5819232c72b97c0ae0`; champion `f56535e29a1c699bb1a1ea59ae6f57f047fda88e`; decision **invalid**.

Weights use inverse summed g_l^2/h_l over primitives sharing atoms, with fixed initial empirical h_l and a numerical floor. Positive fitted slopes propose their gradient root; negative slopes use the current gradient divided by the absolute slope. Unsupported fits use the ordinary quasi-Newton component. Clip each fitted proposal to its observed coordinate range and the current trust bound, project the combined vector to the free tangent space, and enforce the global component bound. Nonfinite, zero or non-descent proposals fall back to the ordinary step. Clear history when the PES/coordinate system resets. Constrained and non-minimization paths use the ordinary step.

Broad slowdown or sustained nonconvergence would contradict this direct adaptation; passive failure traces can distinguish instability, stagnation and slow descent before any bounded repair.

A separate control could measure alignment with a positive diagonal Hessian metric M: c=(e.s)/sqrt((s.M.s)*(e.M^-1.e)). The weighted SR1 term is then (e.s)*outer(e,e)/((s.M.s)*(e.M^-1.e)), retaining the nonsingular zero-alignment limit and exact secant condition when blended with TS-BFGS. Taking M=abs(diag(B)) with only a numerical floor balances current coordinate stiffness without another force call. This changes only the mixing criterion, not the TS-BFGS term; it does not make the entire optimizer invariant. ## Cycle 52: stiffness-scaled alignment for mixed Hessian updates
Candidate `30e1cc5e3c9a7f71ee7ab19047c5aa23e360c6ca`; champion `f56535e29a1c699bb1a1ea59ae6f57f047fda88e`; decision **discard**.

**Change:** Only in `update_H`'s single-secant blend, define M=diag(max(abs(diag(B)),1e-8)). Measure step norm with M and residual norm with M^-1; their dual pairing e.s defines the cosine. Use cosine-squared mixing, writing the SR1 contribution as c/(||s||_M ||e||_M^-1)*outer(e,e) to avoid a residual-dot-step denominator. Preserve the original raw-norm skip guards, TS-BFGS term, multi-secant behavior, early model fitting/replay, geometry, GP and trust policy.
**Derivation:** Under a diagonal coordinate rescaling, M transforms as a Hessian and these primal/dual norms give the same cosine away from the numerical floor. The blended correction still maps s to e and is symmetric. This balances only the mixing criterion, not the entire TS-BFGS algorithm. Weighted least-change norms are discussed in Bofill's analysis https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/jcc.540161103 ; this particular diagonal-metric blend is our adaptation, not a formula attributed to that paper.
**Uncertainty/control:** Diagonal entries in a redundant indefinite Hessian may be poor scale estimates; the accepted Euclidean blend may be empirically better. A cost or energy loss falsifies this particular metric choice without implying weighted norms are generally unhelpful. No floor sweep is planned without evidence.

**Independent collective-prior lead while pending:** Cycle 31's unrestricted contact springs improved cost but failed energy; cycle 32 retained only intracomponent springs. A new, separately bounded hypothesis is to add contact *correlation* within the existing collective block while preserving each primitive's prior diagonal, rather than adding raw spring stiffness. Map intercomponent distance Jacobians into internals, restrict to translation/rotation columns, normalize their Gram matrix to a correlation R, and retain identity rows for unobserved columns. With alpha=1/(1+lambda_max(R)), C=(1-alpha)I+alpha*R has unit diagonal and eigenvalues between 1/2 and 2. Conjugate C by the square roots of the existing collective diagonal and project by the existing P. This replaces only the collective physical-fit block: its scalar fit parameter, overall fit count and all other blocks stay unchanged. It tests contact direction coupling with bounded stiffness, not another raw nonbonded spring strength.
The physical separation is motivated by the combined bonded/nonbonded preconditioners in https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-32105-x , section “Combining FF and Exp preconditioners”; our normalized collective correlation and spectral shrinkage are a different construction. Correlations need not match real attractive interactions, and bounded local stiffness cannot guarantee preserving favorable basins. No implementation or local numerical test has been run.

**Noise-robust update source, not selected:** https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.01275 derives secant-penalized BFGS for corrupted gradient measurements. Current passive traces do not establish gradient noise, and replacing exact secants would need a defensible error estimate. Therefore this source does not presently justify a candidate.

Their residual targets are zero because R is included. The unrelated public geomeTRIC reference implementation https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leeping/geomeTRIC/master/geometric/internal.py uses reference gyration lengths for rotation coordinates (around lines 2251-2262). Our implementation only changes restriction/safety metrics, and does not reproduce their full representation or trust algorithm.

Full gates determine benefit; no size-factor tuning is planned without diagnostic evidence.

## Cycle 92: trace-matched normalized-volume umbrella mode
Champion `71bc71cd0f3fa378394283b4eb42c5596eceece4`; candidate `627d25d2d02330bf9b53a31aba3eef1b045b4ba7`; decision **discard**.

Its Cartesian gradient is cyclic cross(vj,vk)/(r1*r2*r3)-phi*vi/ri^2 for neighbor i, with center gradient minus their sum. Map this one row through the same native Jacobian pseudoinverse. Normalize it to have squared norm equal to the sum of squared norms of that center's existing weighted mapped rows, then replace those rows by this one row. The rank-one trace matching is our proposed prior construction, not a Tinker force field or coefficient. Its gradient is invariant to translations, covariant under rotations, and changes only sign under odd neighbor permutations, so the Gram contribution is permutation invariant. It is orthogonal to independent bond-length scaling. The MolMod module page remains unavailable and supplies no formula here.

The volume gradient vanishes at some extreme orientations, requiring the explicit original-row fallback. No amplitude sweep or physical force-field calculations. Full unchanged gates decide.

## Cycle 258: Positive step-metric correction by secant covariance matching

Hypothesis: matching recent displacement and gradient-change second moments can improve the positive step metric without imposing exact signed secants or changing the symmetric energy model. Source: Xi-Lin Li, Preconditioned Stochastic Gradient Descent, criterion E[dg^T P dg+dx^T P^-1 dx] and solution P Rg P=Rx, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.04202 and https://sites.google.com/site/lixilinx/home/psgd . This is a deterministic regularized adaptation using existing paid secants, not the source's random perturbations, SGD step schedule or stochastic-noise guarantee.

Implementation: collect six recent native transported (s,y) pairs. After six initial calibrated secants, whiten each pair by the current native positive QN model M=V diag(L) V^T: u=sqrt(L)V^T Ufree^T s, v=diag(1/sqrt(L))V^T Ufree^T y. Divide both by sqrt((||u||^2+||v||^2)/2), retaining their relative magnitude and preventing early large pairs from dominating. Use A=I+sum(vv^T), B=I+sum(uu^T), where identity is one isotropic model prior. The positive inverse metric correction T solves T B T=A, with explicit matrix-square-root solution. It is computed only in the rank-at-most-12 span of observations; outside that span the current metric remains. Transform T back to a positive step curvature and use the original spectral-shift trust solver. Symmetric TS learning, energy prediction, GP, geometry and all gates remain unchanged. Singular/nonpositive/nonfinite numerical cases retain the native metric.

This differs from exact symmetric multisecants and soft secant fitting: no signed vector equation P y=s is imposed. Uncertainty: optimization-selected, finite, curved-path secants are biased samples, and the isotropic prior/normalization is our modeling choice. Test this fixed formulation once; a broad loss does not justify prior/window sweeps. A localized passive failure may justify a bounded implementation repair. Static AST and whitespace checks only; all numerical behavior is measured remotely.

Outcome: `499aa41f9e735cbfb3509edebd12d6b1e0f502ae`, train `4a87c914b0a047dba12c2501d97973bc`, cost 0.7659237223115666, energy 1.0012171245911194, all 469 converged, zero errors. ## Cycle 268: Block leave-one-out GP covariance matching

**Hypothesis:** Historical energy/gradient blocks that disagree with predictions from the other paid points can dominate the almost-interpolating GP. Giving these blocks observation covariance proportional to their conditional discrepancy may improve nonlinear proposals without discarding history or changing the kernel. This is model-discrepancy handling; no claim that the physical evaluator returns noisy or corrupted forces.
**Source:** Tang/Zhu/de Jong2021 [primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.11352), section3, relates leave-one-out Gaussian residuals and adaptive observation noise. The block extension and single simultaneous update below are derived here, not the paper's iterative scalar multiplicative algorithm. Robust Student-t and trimmed-likelihood papers were considered but are not implemented.
**Derivation/change:**In `_surrogate_step`, first fit the unchanged kernel K (including1e-7 jitter), alpha=K^-1*t. For each historical point except current, collect its energy plus d directional derivatives as a block of m=d+1 observations. Its conditional covariance given all other blocks is V=(K^-1_ii)^-1 and its residual e=V*alpha_i. In the restricted covariance family (1+lambda)*V, the conditional negative log likelihood is m*log(1+lambda)/2+(e.T*V^-1*e)/(2*(1+lambda))+constant. Its nonnegative minimizer is lambda=max(0,alpha_i.T*V*alpha_i/m-1). Add lambda*V to that observation block, simultaneously using all original conditional estimates, then factor/refit once. Current block retains original jitter and exact posterior value/gradient anchoring. If all lambda=0 retain original factors. SPD/finite guards retain original fit on failure. Query covariance stays latent/noiseless; posterior variance uses the refitted observation matrix. No extra force calls.
**Distinction/limits:**Unlike21/143 this changes pointwise observation reliability rather than common residual amplitude; unlike111/113 it measures actual conditional inconsistency rather than deriving noise solely from tangent misalignment. Unlike255, the physical Hessian fit/replay remains untouched. A single shared-chart block can have correlated energy/gradient mismatch, hence a full PSD noise block rather than independent coordinate weights. Conditional estimates are correlated across blocks; one simultaneous pass is not a joint likelihood optimum. Strongly nonlinear true information may be incorrectly suppressed. Full unchanged gates decide; broad loss defers without inflation/threshold/history sweeps.

## Cycle 295: Burg prior for positive physical calibration

**Hypothesis:**Physical stiffness coefficients describe positive multiplicative ratios. A positive relative-entropy prior may regularize these ratios better than additive Gaussian shrinkage, improving the initial model learned from the first six secants. This is a prior-shape change, not a ridge-strength or observation-window sweep.
**Source/derivation:**Kanamori/Ohara [Bregman quasi-Newton framework](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.2847), section1 equations4–5, motivates the positive discrepancy tr(P*Q^-1)-logdet(P*Q^-1)-n. Applied only to coefficient ratios with reference1, the penalty is ridge*(w-log(w)-1). Its value, gradient and Hessian at1 match the native .5*ridge*(w-1)^2. The molecular feature matrices are not diagonal or independent, so this is a coefficient prior, not a full matrix-invariant divergence. Signed cross-feature coefficients retain their original Gaussian prior centered at0.
**Change/control:**Store the native ridge, recover data-only Gram Q and RHS b, then minimize .5*w.T*Q*w-b.T*w plus the new positive penalties and unchanged signed penalties. Solve the small convex problem with exact cyclic coordinate minimizers, warm-starting from the previous unconstrained solution. A positive coordinate solves a*w^2+(c+ridge)*w-ridge=0; use cancellation-safe branches and hypot. Signed coordinates use their exact linear solution. Require finite positive iterates and relative gradient residual<=1e-10, with a200-sweep bound; otherwise use the original direct quadratic solve. Apply the original .5–2 and signed[-1,1] clips only after solving. This retains the native clipping convention rather than58's joint bound-constrained fit. All six-pair eligibility, secant normalization, physical blocks, ridge strengths, replay, GP and geometry remain244.

## Cycle 303: Cubic geodesic logarithm for GP history

**Hypothesis:**The GP currently treats tangent-projected historical chords as initial geodesic displacements. Curvature contracts those chords at cubic order. For tangent p and v=K*p, set n=N*D(v)*v and c(p)=K.T*D(v).T*n. Tangent projection of exp(s)-q is s-c(s)/6+O(||s||^4); therefore its inverse is log≈p+c(p)/6. Its directional derivative is delta_p+K.T*[D(K*delta_p).T*n+2*D(v).T*N*D(v)*K*delta_p]/6. This is a local polynomial approximation, not an exact finite logarithm or a claim about large-angle paths.

Use151's same declared constants c_kappa=2*d^(1/4),c_sigma=d, with c_delta=1e-5 from the paper's numerical solver accuracy. No benchmark-function execution or parameter selection. Complexity assumptions and molecular global smoothness are not established.
**Physical units:** Initialize430's chemical Hessian without force queries, pull it into Cartesian space, relax dummy coordinates by its Schur complement, and form T0=H0^(-1/2) using the earlier Cartesian controls' .01eV/Angstrom² floor. From the first paid Cartesian gradient g define v=T0.T*g and unit direction u=v/||v||. Let a=.15Angstrom/max_atom_norm(T0*u), T=a*T0 and E*=max(a*||v||,1e-8eV). **Algorithm:** Start B=0. Epoch t uses kappa=2*d^.25*(t+1)^(1/12), K=floor(kappa),sigma=d*(t+1)^(2/3),theta=d/kappa^5. At inner k form a_k=g_k+sum_(i<=k)(2i+1)*g_i/(k+1), solve a_k.s+.5*s.B.s+sigma*||s||4/4 by spectral secular root including the hard case, and make one paid call at x+s. Update B with the full PSB correction scaled by(1-theta)/(1+theta). At each epoch end also evaluate the source weighted coordinate average, charging its actual combined energy/force call and checking external convergence. If not converged, resume the source endpoint and B from cached state without an artificial reevaluation; the next actually paid geometry becomes the returned state. Endpoint/average checks share the fixed200-call budget.

Spectral solves check the source residual condition before calling calc. Source average checks add real overhead. ## Cycle 456: Innovation-adaptive covariance memory for secants

Champion `19ef38c155eee70f9872b95841931f5a303e74c4`.
**Hypothesis:** A Hessian learner that remembers which response directions are already known can preserve useful cross-mode information better than restarting its error metric for every update. Replenishing uncertainty when the measured gradient response exceeds its prediction may accommodate nonquadratic drift without a fixed forgetting window.
**Sources:** Hennig/Kiefel https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume14/hennig13a/hennig13a.pdf section 2, equations 10–12, provides Gaussian secant inference and distinguishes symmetric estimates from symmetric beliefs. Read its symmetry caveat explicitly. https://sites.utexas.edu/near/wp-content/uploads/sites/6030/2022/05/root-1.pdf describes innovation covariance matching for linear filtering. Our symmetric matrix process, one-response moment estimate and native geometry adaptation below are independent derivations; neither source establishes their molecular efficacy.
**Derived model:** In fixed initial physical units A=D^-1/2*H*D^-1/2, assume a symmetric error with Cov(A_ij,A_kl)=(W_ik*W_jl+W_il*W_jk)/2. Start W=I. Normalize z=sqrt(D)*dx and r=(dg-H*dx)/sqrt(D) by the same ||z||. Predicted squared response residual is c=((z.W.z)*tr(W)+||W*z||^2)/2. Inflate the covariance factor to V=W+q*I, choosing the smallest q>=0 for which that trace reaches ||r||². For unit z the quadratic coefficients are a=(n+1)/2, b=(tr(W)+(n+2)*z.W.z)/2, and excess=max(||r||²-c,0); q=2*excess/(b+sqrt(b²+4*a*excess)). Numerical SPD completion only is 64*eps*n*max(lambda_max(W),1). With u=V*z/(z.V.z), the exact symmetric conditional mean correction is r*u.T+u*r.T-(z.r)*u*u.T; lift by sqrt(D) on both sides. Posterior factor Wnew=V-(V*z)*(V*z).T/(z.V.z). This can preserve an indefinite Hessian while its error covariance remains PSD. Eigenvalue clipping of W removes roundoff negatives, not negative physical curvature.
**Change planned:** Replace both native single-secant learning routes by this learner. Each early physical-prior refit starts a fresh W=I and replays the same paid six-pair history; afterwards retain W across updates. Preserve the physical coefficient fit itself, initial 450 model, ordinary negative-spectrum reflection, GP, geodesic path, trust feedback and calculator contract. Unsupported/nonfinite covariance states reset uncertainty and use the existing native update. No new empirical shrinkage, memory, rank, covariance amplitude or response threshold.
**Distinction/uncertainty:** 66/270 used a fixed least-change metric and SR1 blend; 233 used a spatial integral GP with bandwidth/window; 342 compressed Hessian eigenvalues. This tests learned uncertainty memory and innovation-driven renewal with no SR1 mixture. The full redundant native dimension enters the moment model, old observations do not share an exact fixed manifold frame, a single innovation is a noisy variance estimate, and first-six replay resets uncertainty after prior refits. These are modeling limitations, not stochastic-force assumptions. A broad cost/energy failure ends this implementation without covariance, inflation, floor, blend or activation sweeps; passive localized failures plus useful signal are required before at most three bounded repairs.

## Cycle 461: Local shape correlations for bending

Orthogonal pinching preserves the constraint and cannot increase this convex spectral objective; the unconstrained complement is I. Positive completions have c=b²/a+tau². Writing det(A)=a*tau², differentiation gives tau*hypot(1,b/(a+sqrt(a)*tau))=1, a strictly increasing equation with a unique root in(0,1]. Solve by64 bounded bisections. For b=0 take c=1. **Sources:** ASE MDMin primary implementation https://docs.ase-lib.org/_modules/ase/optimize/mdmin.html read; its two half-force updates surround a nonnegative force-parallel velocity projection.
