Normalize x and r by ||x|| for stability. Solve by symmetric eigendecomposition with dimension-scaled64eps rank threshold. Require a finite free-secant residual at1e-8 relative accuracy, else retain native TS/SR1. Add U*R*C*R.T*U.T to the existing H; do not zero or refit old correlations. A complete wrapper rewrite tests this formulation, without a surrogate or paid line search.
**Sources/counterevidence:** Weser https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcc.27029 sections2–4 derives hierarchical frame chain rules and reports worse unconstrained optimization with ordinary Z-matrix treatment. We take this negative evidence seriously: spherical coordinates and diagonal per-coordinate stiffness are not assumed suitable. INRIA https://sbl.inria.fr/doc/Molecular_coordinates-user-manual.html embedding section motivates explicit recursive position construction. Liu https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/cgf.70515 section3.2 describes smooth shortest Rodrigues rotations away from antipodes. Our bond-vector chart and optimizer below are our own adaptation, not an implementation of a molecular algorithm claimed by these papers.
**Chart derivation:** Build one deterministic Prim tree using distance/(sum covalent radii), rooted at the atom nearest centroid; disconnected fragments are connected by the same general rule. Root has Cartesian coordinates. Every other atom has three local bond-vector components q_i, initially x_i-x_parent, with e_i their initial unit direction. Recursively x_i=x_parent+R_parent*q_i, R_i=R_parent*Q(e_i,q_i/||q_i||), Q=I+K+K²/(1+e.u), K=[e cross u]_x. This triangular map retains3N degrees of freedom with invertible orthogonal diagonal blocks, including rings and linear chains; no spherical-angle pole or collinear-reference triad is needed. A frame rotation carries all descendants, but each retains its own unconstrained local vector. Domain guards reject zero-length and antipodal cheap proposals. It is distinct from373/383's interfragment pose replacements and their approximate native history: this chart covers all atoms and stores exact gradients in a single fixed chart.
**Derivatives/metric:** Propagate dx_i=dx_parent+dR_parent*q_i+R_parent*dq_i and dR_i=dR_parent*Q+R_parent*dQ analytically, with du=(I-uuT)dq/r, dQ=dK+(dK*K+K*dK)/(1+e.u)-K²(e.du)/(1+e.u)². No finite-difference derivatives. Initial Cartesian metric is463's native physical Hessian pulled back through its Jacobian and Schur-eliminated dummy coordinates, eigenvalue floor.01 as prior rewrite controls. Let Tcart be its inverse square root; choose T=J0^-1*Tcart and q=q0+T*z. Thus J0*T=Tcart and initial model in z is I, explicitly including every ancestral derivative. Nonstationary coordinate-curvature terms are learned by full-chart gradient secants rather than asserted present in the initial approximation.
**Controller:** Existing native TS/SR1 update on exact z-gradient differences. Reflect learned Hessian eigenvalues, floor1e-8, solve Euclidean trust subproblem by scalar shift (60bisections); radius.2 initially, halve to half-used-step for rho<.25, double for rho>.75 and usednorm>.8radius. Always advance to the paid endpoint as in native controller. At most40cheap halvings enforce actual maxatomic displacement.15Angstrom and native initial-noncontact collision guard. Predict with the positive trust model; no paid trial/rejection restoration, duplicate stopping calls or modified convergence. Wrapper returns exactly last evaluated float64nm and successful call count; stop signals propagate.
**Interpretation/control:** This is a fundamental coherent chart/controller implementation, not an isolated proof that chart selection alone improves463. Full metric conditioning can still become stale, tree paths can distort ring motion, and full-chart TS curvature may be inferior to native transport. No tree/root, rotation-domain, trust-radius, floor or scope sweep after an unexplained broad loss. A localized passive failure with useful signal could justify a bounded repair. No local numerical execution.

## Cycle 682: Integrable scalar-derived Hessian surrogate process

Champion `99a2d8b5482466729ddde624fc4253fc98aba249`.
**Hypothesis:** Enforcing that the inferred spatial Hessian is the second derivative of one scalar field can remove inconsistent curvature directions from676's merely symmetric process, improving finite proposals from the same observed microstep secants.
**Sources/prerequisite:** de Roos/Gessner/Hennig https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/de-roos21a/de-roos21a.pdf sections2.1,3,4.1 (linear-operator GP closure and Hessian inference); JetGP https://samm-py.github.io/jetgp/theory/derivative_enhanced_gaussian_processes.html equation7 (fourth-derivative Hessian covariance). This independently derived integrable field meets676's explicit model prerequisite. It is a structural covariance replacement, not a passive diagnosis of676 or a ridge/bandwidth sweep.
**Derivation:** Let H(x)=I+Hess(psi(x)), psi a scalar SE process with k(r)=exp(-lambda*||r||²/2)/(3lambda²), lambda=.25. This preserves676's unit diagonal Hessian variance and spatial length; the implied offdiagonal variance1/3 and cross-diagonal covariance1/3 are forced by the scalar model, replacing676's offdiagonal1/2 and independent diagonals. For u,v and r=x-z, set a=r.u,b=r.v,c=u.v. The contracted fourth derivative is C(r,u,v)=exp(-lambda*r²/2)/3 times [cI+uvT+vuT-lambda*(b*(urT+ruT)+a*(vrT+rvT)+abI+c*rrT)+lambda²*ab*rrT]. It equals Cov(H(x)u,H(z)v). Full fourth-tensor index symmetry means the same expression C(r,u,alpha) contracts Cov(H(point),H(segment)u) against observation coefficient alpha.

Keep normalized observations (gnew-gold)/length-unit, priorI, five-point positive Gauss-Legendre, ridge1e-7, all accepted segments, reflected eigenvalues floor1e-4, strongWolfe1e-4/.9 max20,12accepted/200cached queries/gtolInfinity1e-5. ## Cycle 710: Rational-gradient interpolation in surrogate line search
**Hypothesis:** A rational fit to all directional-gradient observations can locate a useful stationary ray point when cubic interpolation is inaccurate, improving finite BFGS proposals without extra paid forces.
**Source:** Nakatsukasa/Sete/Trefethen https://arxiv.org/pdf/1612.00337, sections2–4. Use greedy support selection and the smallest right singular vector of the Loewner matrix; derivative samples are the scalar data, not confluent Hermite constraints. This is our line-search adaptation, not a published AAA optimizer.
**Change/control:** Replace only GP microsearch with inverse BFGS plus strong-Wolfe expansion/zoom. During zoom, fit normalized observed ray derivatives with at most min(6,n//2) barycentric supports; choose a positive-slope real numerator root within the central80% of the bracket. Invalid/pole-adjacent fits use midpoint. Every proposed root must pass the exact GP Wolfe test. Unit initial ray step, c1=1e-4,c2=.9, at most20 ray queries,12 accepted BFGS steps,200 total cached model queries,1e-5 gradient tolerance. Domain failures bound the bracket. Preserve GP fit, ordinary initialization, physical model, paid steps and all critics. The general BFGS controls match the prior683 experiment; its Bayesian acquisition is not reused.
**Limits/falsifier:** AAA approximates gradients between sampled points without a global error guarantee. No degree, tolerance, bracket, budget or critic sweep after an unexplained loss. Full train/validation gates against463 apply. No local optimizer/model numerical execution.
**Static verification:** Syntax and diff whitespace pass; AST changes confined to new helper and microsearch call. Reviewed Loewner sign, normalized data/ray conversion, support exclusion, bounded degree, rational derivative sign at numerator roots, positive-curvature inverse-BFGS algebra, Wolfe zoom orientation and query-limit handling. Failed trials cannot replace the accepted point. Source-norm constraint uses the unit singular vector (the paper), not the inconsistent sum-of-weights statement in SciPy's prose. No numerical execution.

## Cycle 711: Interval-Hessian surrogate preconditioning
**Hypothesis:** Region-wide curvature bounds can choose stable preconditioners and reuse them until the surrogate iterate leaves that region, improving finite proposals over pointwise BFGS.
**Source/prerequisite:** Sharma et al. https://arxiv.org/html/2510.22342v1, equations3.4–3.8/3.19 and Algorithms1–4. Earlier source audits deferred INTHOP because sampled Hessian extrema cannot bound a region. This implementation supplies interval second-order propagation through scalar bending maps plus the closed analytic GP Hessian, not finite-difference extrema.
**Derivation:** For warped features xi(y)=y+E.T*(c(Ay)-Ay), J=I+E.T*diag(c'-1)*A. Each posterior term is exp(-lambda*diff²/2)*(a+b.diff), where b=lambda*Kmap*w_gradient. Its feature gradient is k*(b-lambda*l*diff); Hessian k*((lambda²*diff*diff.T-lambda*I)*l-lambda*(diff*b.T+b*diff.T)). Pull back via J.T*H*J and add A.T*diag(c''*(E*g_feature))*A. Add unit prior and exact nonlinear bending remainder Hessian. Linear origin anchoring terms have zero Hessian.
**Controller:** INTHOP:F with source initial width.1, Gershgorin interval eigenvalue lower bound, uniform nonnegative shift, source Armijo1e-3/halving/unit initial step; twelve accepted microsteps and200 total model/curvature queries. Restrict box width analytically only to keep all angles strictly inside the existing model domain. Reuse curvature while inside its box; recompute after exit. Tiny machine-relative positive shift makes the source's semidefinite construction invertible. Use max(0,-lambda) for total Hessian shift (correcting source3.24's min typo consistently with3.8). Preserve original GP, physical machinery and all critics.
**Numerical limits:** Elementary arithmetic uses outward nextafter rounding; sums accumulate interval additions. Transcendental endpoints rely on NumPy libm with outward padding, so this is not a formally verified interval package. The finite controller claims no source convergence guarantee. Interval dependency may overestimate curvature and slow progress. No width/shift/bounds/Armijo/work sweep without useful signal and localized evidence. No local numerical execution.
**Static review:** Syntax, whitespace, recursive global-symbol audit and outside-helper AST identity pass. Reviewed scalar jet product/reciprocal/square/sine/tanh/sqrt chain rules; support-free batch shapes, zero-angle cases and interval matrix multiplication; feature-space affine-kernel gradient/Hessian signs; bending and warped-coordinate second derivatives; Gershgorin shift and retained-matrix domain. The closed expression includes both warp Hessian contraction and nonlinear mean remainder. Endpoint anchor energy/gradient terms are linear and correctly absent from the Hessian. Failed bounds/trials return only a previously accepted model point. No numerical interval, differentiation, model or optimizer tests executed locally.

**Further source audit while711 pending:** Skjal/Westerlund https://users.abo.fi/twesterl/some-selected-papers/14.%20JOGO-AS-TW-2014.pdf sections2.1–2.4 describes interval-Hessian convex underestimators for branch-and-bound. This suggests a distinct future use of the new interval capability: bounds directing global surrogate exploration, not another shift/width variant of INTHOP. It requires a justified compact search region and a bounded search strategy before implementation. Kothari/Kopanicakova/Krause https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.14780 equations4–9 offers nonlinear overlapping local corrections and a first-order-consistent coarse correction. Applying this directly to paid forces would incur many subproblem calls; a useful cheap coarse model/partition is not established, and398 already tested a different coarse-map Broyden approach. No standalone physical Schwarz candidate selected yet.

## Cycle 712: Interval lower bounds for surrogate initialization
**Hypothesis:** Region lower bounds can direct a small deterministic search toward a better GP basin before the ordinary BFGS refinement, reducing paid steps without conservative curvature damping.
**Source:** Skjal/Westerlund https://users.abo.fi/twesterl/some-selected-papers/14.%20JOGO-AS-TW-2014.pdf sections1–2 motivates Hessian-bound-guided branch-and-bound. Our bound is a simpler Taylor quadratic: if Hess(f)>=lambda*I throughout a box, f(c+s)>=f(c)+g(c).s+.5*lambda*||s||². Its box minimum separates by coordinate, including negative lambda. This is not the full alphaBB convex relaxation solver.
**Controlled construction:** Reuse711's exact committed interval helper unchanged. Search a cube around the physical origin inside the existing GP length-two ball; shrink analytically to keep all active angles within their existing domain. The ordinary initial point remains an incumbent even if outside this exploratory cube. At each node query its center, compute the interval lower bound, and query the bound minimizer; best-bound-first bisection of a longest edge, at most12 splits. Then run the original12-step/1e-5 BFGS from the best observed initialization. Bound total objective and interval queries to200 and preserve last accepted BFGS iterate on interruption. No claim of completed global minimization or rigorous floating-point certification. Existing physical, model and proposal gates remain unchanged.
**Distinction/limits:** This tests a new use of interval information, not a width/shift/Armijo adjustment to711. It differs from495's DIRECT seed by using the newly constructed region curvature information. Overly loose bounds or a small finite tree may provide no useful initialization. No split count/domain/bound/refinement/critic sweep after unexplained loss. No local numerical tests.
**Static verification:** Syntax, whitespace, recursive global-symbol audit pass. AST confirms the interval helper is identical to711; other changes are global initializer and its caller only. Rechecked signed quadratic box minimizer, Gershgorin lower bound, domain halfwidth, bisection coverage, serial heap tie-breaker, incumbent pruning,200-query limit and BFGS accepted-point callback. Source interval limitations remain; no local numeric tests executed.
